title: Break-even analysis
examples: What is the difference between fixed and variable costs?
How do I use the break-even chart to find the point?
If we increase our selling price, does the break-even point change?

explain.say: Today we learn about break-even analysis in business.

items: It finds where profit is zero.

explain.say: First we must understand the formula for the break-even point.
Fixed costs are expenses that do not change with output level.
Variable costs change depending on how many items you produce.
Next we look at the break-even chart to visualise this point.
The margin of safety tells us how much sales can drop before losing money.

faq.a: Fixed costs are expenses that you have to pay no matter how much you produce. For example, your monthly rent is a fixed cost.
asks: Are fixed costs always the same?
What costs are not affected by production?

faq.q: How do I calculate the break-even point in units?
faq.a: You use the formula: fixed costs divided by the price minus the variable cost per unit. This gives you the number of units needed to sell.
asks: What is the formula for BEP?
How do I find the break-even output?

faq.q: What does the margin of safety represent?
faq.a: The margin of safety is the amount by which actual sales can fall before the business starts making a loss. It shows your safety cushion.
asks: Is margin of safety about profit?
How much can sales drop safely?

faq.q: Do I need to know the selling price for the chart?
faq.a: Yes, you need the selling price to draw the total revenue line on the chart. This line shows all the money coming in.
asks: Is selling price important for the chart?
What goes on the revenue line?

faq.q: If I increase my fixed costs, what happens to the break-even point?
faq.a: If fixed costs increase, the break-even point will also increase, assuming everything else stays the same. You need to sell more just to cover rent.
asks: Does more rent mean more sales needed?
How does fixed cost affect BEP?

facts: The break-even point is the level of output where total revenue equals total costs.
Fixed costs remain constant regardless of the volume of goods produced.
The margin of safety is calculated by subtracting the break-even sales from actual sales.
If a business sells nothing, its loss will equal its total fixed costs.

quiz.say: A business has fixed costs of one hundred pounds, a selling price of ten pounds, and variable costs of five pounds per unit. What is the break-even point in units?
quiz.why: The formula is fixed costs divided by the contribution per unit, which is ten minus five, giving you twenty units.

wrong.0: This mistake happens if you divide fixed costs by the selling price only.
wrong.1: This mistake happens if you add the fixed costs and variable costs together.
wrong.2: This mistake happens if you only calculate the contribution per unit.

quiz.say: A company expects to sell one thousand items. If the break-even point is found at 700 units, what is the margin of safety?
quiz.show: Margin of Safety = Actual Sales - BEP
quiz.why: The margin of safety is the difference between the expected sales of one thousand and the break-even point of seven hundred units.

wrong.0: This mistake happens if you incorrectly assume the margin of safety equals the break-even point.
wrong.1: This mistake happens if you assume that any difference means no safety cushion.
wrong.3: This mistake happens if you add the actual sales and the break-even point together.

quiz.say: If a business increases its rent, which cost category is increasing?
quiz.why: Rent is a payment that must be made regularly and does not change based on how many items are sold, so it is a fixed cost.

wrong.0: Revenue is money earned from sales, not an expense.
wrong.2: Variable costs change with production, like materials used.
wrong.3: While it increases total costs, it specifically affects the fixed portion.
